instruction:

word/document.xml: SOW 111 for Agreement to Perform Consulting Services to Rock Castle Construction

This Statement of Work (SOW) is issued pursuant to the Consultant Services Master Agreement between Rock Castle Construction (“Client”) and Widgets, Inc. (“Contractor”), effective 6/17/24 (the “Agreement”). This SOW is subject to the terms and conditions contained in the Agreement between the parties and is made a part thereof. Any term not otherwise defined herein shall have the meaning specified in the Agreement. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the terms of this SOW and the terms of this Agreement, the terms of this SOW shall govern and prevail.

This SOW # 111 (hereinafter called the “SOW”), effective as of 6/17/24, is entered into by and between Contractor and Client, and is subject to the terms and conditions specified below. The Exhibit(s) to this SOW, if any, shall be deemed to be a part hereof. In the event of any inconsistencies between the terms of the body of this SOW and the terms of the Exhibit(s) hereto, the terms of the body of this SOW shall prevail.
The Services shall commence on 6/17/24, and shall continue through 6/17/25.
1 Widget Engineer to assist in the widget installation and configuration at 40 hours of labor.
Contractor shall provide the Services and Deliverable(s) as follows:
Installation and configuration of 100 Wonder Widgets at the client site, with assistance from one Widget Engineer. The installation will include configuration and verification of the widgets.

The deliverables include the installed and configured Wonder Widgets and documentation of the work performed. Contractor will provide the client with the information required to operate the widgets after installation.

Contractor will provide the engagement resources identified above, perform the agreed services, and provide documentation of the project work performed. Contractor will coordinate the installation schedule with the Client Project Manager.

Client will provide access to the installation location at 123 Somewhere St., Wherever, MI 48001. Client will ensure that the location is ready for installation and designate a project manager to coordinate access and acceptance of the services.

This engagement will be conducted on a Time & Materials basis. The total value for the Services pursuant to this SOW shall not exceed the agreed amount unless otherwise agreed to by both parties via the project change control procedure, as outlined within. A PCR will be issued specifying the amended value.
This figure is based on 40 hours of professional services. Contractor will provide up to 1 resource based on the following functional/rate structure.

Upon completion of this Performance Period, Contractor and Client will have the option to renew this agreement for an additional then-stated number of hours at the then-current hourly rate for those resources identified.
Client will be invoiced monthly for the consulting services and T&L expenses. Standard Contractor invoicing is assumed to be acceptable. Invoices are due upon receipt.

Client will be invoiced all costs associated with out-of-pocket expenses (including, without limitation, costs and expenses associated with meals, lodging, local transportation and any other applicable business expenses) listed on the invoice as a separate line item. Reimbursement for out-of-pocket expenses in connection with performance of this SOW, when authorized and up to the limits set forth in this SOW, shall be in accordance with Client’s then-current published policies governing travel and associated business expenses, which information shall be provided by the Client Project Manager. The limit of reimbursable expenses pursuant to this SOW is estimated to be 15% of the fees unless otherwise authorized in writing and agreed to by both parties via the project change control procedure outlined within.

Invoices shall be submitted monthly in arrears, referencing this Client’s SOW Number to the address indicated above. Each invoice will reflect charges for the time period being billed and cumulative figures for previous periods.

Terms of payment for each invoice are due upon receipt by Client of a proper invoice. Contractor shall provide Client with sufficient details to support its invoices, including time sheets for services performed and expense receipts and justifications for authorized expenses, unless otherwise agreed to by the parties. Payments for services invoiced that are not received within 30 days from date of invoice will be subject to a 5% penalty per calendar month.
Contractor shall have fulfilled its obligations when any one of the following first occurs:

•  Contractor accomplishes the Contractor activities described within this SOW, including delivery to Client of the materials listed in the Section entitled “Deliverable Materials,” and Client accepts such activities and materials without unreasonable objections. No response from Client within 2 business days of deliverables being delivered by Contractor is deemed acceptance.
•  Contractor and/or Client has the right to cancel services or deliverables not yet provided with 20 business days advance written notice to the other party.
Client will provide the access and resources necessary for Contractor to perform the agreed work. Any work outside the scope of this SOW will be subject to the project change control procedure.
The following process will be followed if a change to this SOW is required:
•  A Project Change Request (PCR) will be the vehicle for communicating change. The PCR must describe the change, the rationale for the change, and the effect the change will have on the project.
•  The designated Project Manager of the requesting party (Contractor or Client) will review the proposed change and determine whether to submit the request to the other party.

•  Both Project Managers will review the proposed change and approve it for further investigation or reject it. Contractor and Client will mutually agree upon any charges for such investigation, if any. If the investigation is authorized, the Client Project Managers will sign the PCR, which will constitute approval for the investigation charges. Contractor will invoice Client for any such charges. The investigation will determine the effect that the implementation of the PCR will have on SOW price, schedule and other terms and conditions of the Agreement.
•  Upon completion of the investigation, both parties will review the impact of the proposed change and, if mutually agreed, a Change Authorization will be executed.
•  A written Change Authorization and/or PCR must be signed by both parties to authorize implementation of the investigated changes.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties hereto have caused this SOW to be effective as of the day, month and year first written above.

explanation.purpose: Establish what the finished text should say. The packaged Python inspector opens the starter DOCX, counts its revision tags and reads each paragraph with insertions retained and deletions omitted.
explanation.result: The starter has 14 insertions and 13 deletions. Its 84 body paragraphs in that accepted form supply the expected text for comparison with the saved document.

example.title: Reproduce the paragraph comparison
example.instruction: Run this Python example in the trial’s verifier folder to compare the two recorded inspections.
example.code:
import json
from pathlib import Path

paragraphs = {}
for line in Path("live-observations.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
    observation = json.loads(line)
    view = observation.get("view")
    if view in ("starter_document", "document") and observation["ok"]:
        data = json.loads(observation["data"])
        paragraphs[view] = data["text_with_revisions_accepted"]["word/document.xml"]

expected = paragraphs["starter_document"]
saved = paragraphs["document"]
print(f"Expected paragraphs: {len(expected)}")
print(f"Saved paragraphs: {len(saved)}")
print(f"Identical text: {expected == saved}")

title: Complete and Sign a Clinical Note
summary: Complete encounter findings, assessment, and plan, then sign the note.
instruction:
You are a clinician completing the encounter documentation for patient Gandalf Greyhame Wiz regarding his presentation of abdominal pain.

Update the clinical note for his encounter with the visit findings, assessment, and plan. Record gastrointestinal abdominal pain in the Review of Systems, and document right lower quadrant (RLQ) abdominal tenderness on the physical exam along with a comment on the abdominal exam noting possible appendicitis. In the assessment, summarize his presentation with abdominal pain and the impression of possible appendicitis. In the plan, order a CBC with differential and note possible appendicitis along with a consultation with Dr. Mayfield to determine whether an appendectomy is the appropriate course of action.

Once the documentation is complete, sign and lock the clinical note as the rendering provider.

rubrics.criterion: Gandalf Greyhame Wiz's encounter clinical note records abdominal pain as a positive gastrointestinal finding in the Review of Systems

title: Update Class Gradebook

instruction:
Grade and return the requested "Week 1: Writing" work in the "Organize and Educate" course, then export and annotate the updated class gradebook.

For "Week 1: Writing", assess Casey Boehm's turned-in submission using the attached Writing Rubric for a total score of 7/8:  
- Sentence Writing: 2/2  
- Organization: 2/2  
- Punctuation: 2/2  
- Spelling: 1/2

Post the individual private comment "Awesome work sounding out your words and using sight words!" on that turned-in submission before returning work. Return three of the four "Week 1: Writing" roster records—both Casey Boehm entries (the turned-in submission and the unsubmitted entry) and Hannah Koenig's entry—with the shared private comment "Super sentence writing!" while leaving Caitie Instone's entry unreturned.

Once the "Week 1: Writing" grading and returns are complete, export all course grades for "Organize and Educate" into a complete class gradebook. Because this environment produces a local spreadsheet workbook rather than generating a live online spreadsheet, save the updated gradebook at `/home/ga/Documents/Grades Organize and Educate 08-06-2020.ods` and add the comment "Needs to make corrections" to cell D7 in that workbook.

title: Prepare Survey Data and Frequency Analyses
summary: Prepare survey records and compare complete and missing-response frequencies.
instruction:
You are a research analyst preparing a pilot survey dataset and a missing-response reporting check for a study on teacher emotional support and student emotional engagement. Using the questionnaire at `/home/ga/Documents/Teacher Support Study/Document1.docx` as your reference, set up a clean, populated survey dataset and produce comparative demographic frequency analyses under complete and missing-response conditions.

Structure the dataset in your statistical workspace around the individual closed-ended demographic questions and main-study statements in the questionnaire, clearing any stray placeholder entries that may be present. Each item needs a clearly identifiable variable, a descriptive label that accurately reflects the questionnaire item, and an appropriate measurement level distinguishing categorical demographics from ordered scale statements. Assign consistent whole-number codes with value labels for all printed response options, preserving the directional order of the agreement scale, and populate six sample respondent records with varied, valid coded responses across all questionnaire items.

Deliver two sets of frequency analyses covering all demographic variables from the questionnaire so the research team can compare how a missing entry affects reported counts and percentages. Each analysis should report valid and missing case summaries alongside labeled category frequency tables:  
- **Complete Baseline:** Frequency results across all six complete respondent records, showing six valid cases and zero missing cases for every demographic variable.  
- **Missing-Response Comparison:** Frequency results for the same six respondent records with a single respondent's gender response missing and all other demographic entries unchanged, showing five valid cases and one missing case for gender while every other demographic variable retains all six valid cases.

Leave the prepared dataset and both sets of frequency results open in your workspace for review, ensuring the reported distributions are consistent with the respondent records.

rubrics.criterion: The pilot survey dataset contains a clearly identifiable variable for the questionnaire's Gender item.
rubrics.description: Full credit if an actual dataset variable unambiguously represents the questionnaire's Gender item. Any clearly identifiable variable name and position are acceptable; separately opening the reference document is not required. Partial credit if a candidate variable exists but its Gender identity is ambiguous. No credit if the variable is absent or merely proposed. If an evidenced dataset-access or workspace limitation prevents this state, record the uncontrollable blocker in reality_notes or the scoring justification and credit only the verifiable resulting state. A blocker report alone does not satisfy this outcome; failure with available, controllable dependencies remains an agent-controllable shortfall.

title: Edit a YouTube Video with Visual Effects
summary: Assemble an editable presenter video with cutaways, graphics, and music.
instruction:
You are a video editor preparing an editable YouTube video project, "Justin Edit," for presenter Justin Brown.

Include the complete source footage package from `/home/ga/Desktop/Video Assets/` and the soundtrack `/home/ga/Downloads/ES_San Pedro - Sugoi.mp3` in the project so all supplied media remains organized and available for review and follow-on edits. Assemble the main cut in a sequence named "YouTube" matched to the primary presenter camera footage. Trim the unedited setup at the head and tail and cut out interior mistakes, false starts, or dead air so the spoken delivery flows smoothly without gaps.

Introduce the speaker near the opening with an on-screen lower-third graphic reading "JUSTIN BROWN," and layer the supplied ocean and waterfall footage as visual cutaways where they support the presenter's remarks without interrupting the spoken dialogue. Run the background music track across the full edited sequence, aligned cleanly to the end of the cut, while keeping spoken dialogue and music separated and balanced for clear speech. Follow `/workspace/assets/justin_edit_visual_reference.md` for the detailed visual and audio treatments across the edit.

Prepare the project for "YouTube 2160p 4K Ultra HD" export upon approval, and deliver the completed editable project at `/home/ga/Documents/Justin Edit/Justin Edit.kdenlive` (no rendered video file is required at this stage).

rubrics.criterion: Justin Edit retains a usable, editable YouTube sequence with practical access to revise the presenter edit and the placement and timing of its cutaways and opening name graphic.
rubrics.description: Full credit if usable timeline structure preserves practical revision of the opening, closing and interior presenter edits, cutaway placement and timing, and lower-third placement and timing, with the supplied sources available for follow-on edits. Accept equivalent nested or shared structures, linked assets, precomposed graphics and source-derived intermediate media when practical project editability is preserved. Independently editable lettering, background geometry and original framing, color or cutaway-treatment parameters are not required. Partial credit if useful editing structure remains but required main-cut components or source access need repair sufficiently to obstruct follow-on edits. Unused source media outside the main sequence does not reduce credit. No credit if no usable editable main cut remains or the result consists only of flattened final output without usable editing structure. Saving and delivery are assessed separately.

title: Plan a Website Launch and Manage Team Tasks
summary: Organize a team, plan a holiday website launch, and manage handoffs.
instruction:
You are a project manager setting up internal team operations and preparing a holiday website launch for Apple.

The MinorCo workspace needs a new Marketing team that includes Warwick Palm alongside you. In the Asana Demo workspace, set up a workspace-accessible "Apple - Website Design" project where Warwick Palm and Lindsay Amoroso have editing access. Its project overview should capture the scope and business goal: designing a new website for Apple that must be live before Christmas to increase conversion rates and help sell more iPhones this holiday season.

Across client onboarding, design and planning, production, and go-live and final delivery, the project plan should make clear who owns each task across the team, when work is scheduled, how multi-part deliverables break down into subtasks, which approval and readiness milestones matter, and which tasks or testing milestones depend on earlier handoffs. Leave the production milestone for completed page designs open and ask Warwick Palm in its discussion to review the designs you have completed. Publish an on-track status update letting the team know the project is progressing well to finish before Christmas and summarizing the remaining incomplete tasks by assignee.

Keep your personal task list in Asana Demo organized by section with "Recently assigned" cleared, moving "Planning session with client" along with your newly assigned project commitments into "Upcoming". In MinorCo, follow up on two team updates: add a thumbs-up reaction to Warwick Palm's latest comment on "Troubleshoot: Pipedrive Document sync settings" and archive that notification once addressed, and express appreciation for Kayla Campos's completion of "Session #3 Team Follow Up" in its task discussion.

rubrics.criterion: A newly created team named Marketing exists in the MinorCo workspace.
rubrics.description: Full credit for a saved new team or equivalent native group named exactly Marketing and associated with MinorCo. Partial credit for a saved new intended marketing team with a naming or workspace error. No credit for confirmed noncreation or an uncommitted setup. Unverified state remains unresolved rather than automatically receiving no credit. arguments.command:
python3 -c '
import psycopg2

conn = psycopg2.connect("postgres://openproject:[redacted]@172.17.0.2/openproject")
cur = conn.cursor()

# Check groups
cur.execute("SELECT id, lastname, type FROM users WHERE type LIKE \x27%Group%\x27;")
print("Groups:", cur.fetchall())

# Check group users
cur.execute("SELECT * FROM group_users;")
print("Group users:", cur.fetchall())

# Check members table
cur.execute("SELECT m.id, m.user_id, u.lastname, m.project_id, p.name FROM members m JOIN users u ON m.user_id=u.id JOIN projects p ON m.project_id=p.id;")
print("Members:")
for r in cur.fetchall():
    print(" ", r)

# Check roles
cur.execute("SELECT id, name, position, assignable FROM roles;")
print("Roles:", cur.fetchall())
'

title: Manage Sales Leads and Build Revenue Dashboards
summary: Manage converted leads and build closed-won revenue reports and dashboards.
instruction:
You are a sales operations specialist setting up a new sales workspace and revenue tracking for Call Solutions LLC. Register and activate your workspace account through email verification using the following profile details:  
 - Name: Emily Call  
 - Role: Developer  
 - Company: Call Solutions LLC  
 - Email: [sfemilycall@gmail.com](mailto:sfemilycall@gmail.com)  
 - Username: [EEC@callcompany.com](mailto:EEC@callcompany.com)  
 - Location: Utah, United States, 98002

Within the sales workspace, client ABC's deal records should reflect the conversion of Jane Doe's Web lead in the Education industry, linking the ABC account and Jane Doe's contact record to the $100,000 "ABC- Initial Contract" opportunity at the Closed Won stage. Record John Doe as an additional contact under the ABC account.

For ongoing pipeline management, set up a private "My Open Leads" view showing only your active, unconverted leads and excluding any closed or converted records.

For team-wide revenue visibility, prepare a public "Closed Won Opportunities" report summarizing total closed-won opportunity revenue across all close dates, grouped by lead source. Keep the detail columns focused by including the last modified date while omitting owner role, age, and next step, and include a donut chart breaking down closed-won revenue by lead source.

Build a private companion dashboard named "Closed Won Dashboard" sourced from that report, displaying both an overall closed-won revenue metric and a donut chart breakdown by lead source with current figures loaded across all components (including the closed ABC contract). Set up a dashboard email subscription to deliver updates every Monday at 7:00 AM.

title: Draft a Floor Plan and Architectural Details
summary: Complete a ground-floor drawing and prepare scaled presentation sheets.
instruction:
You are an architectural drafter preparing a ground-floor plan and detail documentation package. Continue `/home/ga/Documents/CAD/floor plan exercise.dwg` in meters, following `/home/ga/Documents/CAD/floor plan exercise reference.pdf` as the design reference for the floor plan geometry, circulation, fixtures, room identities, and architectural details.

Organize the drawing cleanly across dedicated layers for building elements, fixtures, room labels, dimensions, and non-plotting viewports. Build reusable components with interactive controls where elements repeat across varied layouts: flippable single-door and private-restroom assemblies for opposing orientations, a symmetrical double-door component, and an adjustable-width window component that fits the varying opening widths. Label all rooms and residential units, and dimension the exterior plan and the sheeted details in meters using annotative dimensions scaled for their respective views.

Prepare two presentation sheets with rectangular sheet borders, title blocks, and hidden (non-plotting) viewport frames:  
- `Layout1`: Present the ground-floor plan at `1:200`. Complete the title block with `Project`, `Location`, `Drawing name`, `Drawn`, `Scale`, and `Date` fields, recording Project `Example 1`, Drawing name `Ground floor`, and Scale `1:200`.  
- `details`: Present two dimensioned detail views side by side—the single-door detail at `1:16` and the window/profile detail at `1:10`.

Save the completed editable drawing in place at `/home/ga/Documents/CAD/floor plan exercise.dwg` and publish the `Layout1` ground-floor sheet as a PDF at `/home/ga/Documents/CAD/example 2.pdf`.
